headline: Texas Sues OpenAI — and seeks court approval for new AI models before Texans can use them
summary: Texas's lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman personally demands a court-appointed evaluator approve all new AI models before they can be released in the state, a move that could effectively set a national pre-release standard.
details: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a 67-page lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman personally, seeking over $1 million in relief and civil penalties. The core demand of the suit is for a court-appointed evaluator to approve new AI models before their release in Texas.

This proposed remedy is forward-looking, acting as a pre-release veto over what OpenAI can ship to Texans. It raises significant questions about who appoints the evaluator, the standards for approval, and whether a Texas-only order could effectively set a de facto national release standard.

Texas is the second state, following Florida, to name Altman personally in a lawsuit, alleging he directed conduct and overruled employees on safety testing for GPT-4o. The petition even opens with a 2015 quote from Altman about AI's potential to end the world.

Personal liability changes incentives in a way corporate fines do not; a CEO named in a petition cannot simply price a penalty into a roadmap. The lawsuit cites allegations of ChatGPT's involvement in a 16-year-old's suicide plan and drug advice leading to a 19-year-old's fatal overdose.

These are currently allegations, not findings, with no court rulings or hearing dates set. OpenAI has stated it worked with experts on safeguards and is committed to collaborating with states on industry-wide policy, but has not addressed the specific charges.

The petition also alleges tens of thousands of Texas users under 13 and a lack of proper parental identity verification, violating the SCOPE Act. It further claims a teen was able to spend an hour discussing self-harm with ChatGPT without generating a single parental alert.

The lawsuit's political context includes AG Paxton running for the U.S. Senate, with Elon Musk—an OpenAI co-founder and xAI rival—being a significant donor to his campaign. Notably, Texas has not taken action against Musk's xAI, whose Grok has faced criticism.

Texas is now the tenth state to sue OpenAI, following similar child-safety claims from eight other states and Florida's lawsuit in June. This multi-state front shifts the debate from post-fact punishment for chatbot actions to pre-release approval for new AI models.

While nothing changes for ChatGPT users today, the lawsuit poses a new, critical question for all AI labs globally: who ultimately decides if a model is safe enough to ship—the company itself, or a judge?

headline: Touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro launches this week, here’s how the lineup will look
summary: Apple is reportedly reversing its long-standing policy against touchscreens on laptops. This new MacBook Pro is expected to feature an OLED display, marking a significant shift in its product strategy.
details: Apple is reportedly set to introduce a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro this week, a major departure from its long-held stance against touch-enabled laptops. This move would mark the first time a MacBook features a touch display, integrating a technology previously reserved for iPads.

The new models are expected to feature vibrant OLED screens, enhancing visual clarity and color accuracy for professional users. This upgrade aligns with industry trends towards more interactive and visually superior laptop displays.

Sources suggest that this launch will also redefine the MacBook Pro lineup, potentially introducing new configurations or form factors. The integration of touch functionality could open up new possibilities for macOS applications and user interaction.

This strategic shift by Apple is seen as a response to evolving market demands and competition, offering users greater versatility. It represents a significant update to the MacBook Pro series, which has traditionally focused on performance and a non-touch experience.
